vignette: 74-year-old woman with COPD (ICD-10-CM J44.9) seen in her pulmonologist's office for worsening fatigue and morning headaches. The pulmonologist ordered pulse oximetry, which office staff performed under her supervision with the patient seated at rest breathing room air: SpO2 88%. The pulmonologist reviewed the result the same day and prescribes a home stationary oxygen concentrator at 2 L/min. She has no angina, peripheral vascular disease, or terminal illness.
rationale_note: Boundary: SpO2 exactly 88% at rest on room air, ordered, evaluated, and supervised by the treating practitioner.

vignette: 79-year-old man hospitalized for a COPD exacerbation with pneumonia. The day before discharge, his attending physician ordered an arterial blood gas at rest on room air, run by the hospital's certified blood gas laboratory: PaO2 54 mm Hg. A ward pulse oximetry reading taken at the same time showed SpO2 90%. The attending physician reviewed both, documented reliance on the blood gas, and prescribes home oxygen at discharge. He is not terminally ill and has no angina or peripheral vascular disease.
rationale_note: ABG from a certified hospital lab the day before discharge qualifies; conflicting ward oximetry is outweighed because ABG is preferred.

vignette: 71-year-old man with obesity hypoventilation and COPD. His primary care physician ordered resting room-air pulse oximetry, performed in her office under her supervision during a period of worsening daytime somnolence: SpO2 89%. A CBC the same week shows hematocrit 57% (erythrocythemia). There is no dependent edema and an echocardiogram shows normal pulmonary pressures. She reviewed the results and prescribes home oxygen.
rationale_note: Group II boundary: SpO2 exactly 89% with hematocrit 57% (> 56%).

vignette: 68-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer to both lungs and a malignant pleural effusion, enrolled in hospice with a life expectancy of weeks. She has progressive dyspnea at rest. Her hospice physician ordered and personally performed resting room-air pulse oximetry at a home visit: SpO2 85%. He evaluated the result and prescribes home oxygen.
rationale_note: Terminal illness that affects breathing (lung metastases) with qualifying resting hypoxemia; the hospice setting is a distractor.

vignette: 76-year-old man with chronic stable angina who has chest pressure two to three times a week on exertion, relieved by nitroglycerin. His cardiologist ordered and evaluated an arterial blood gas at rest on room air (PaO2 82 mm Hg) and an exercise oximetry test (lowest SpO2 95%). He has no lung disease. The cardiologist prescribes home oxygen to use during angina episodes.
rationale_note: Angina without hypoxemia is a national non-coverage.

vignette: 70-year-old woman with deconditioning and anxiety who reports breathlessness when climbing stairs. Physician-ordered testing, evaluated by her internist, shows SpO2 95% at rest on room air, a lowest SpO2 of 93% during a 6-minute walk, and no desaturation below 92% on overnight oximetry. Echocardiogram shows normal right heart size and pulmonary pressures; there is no edema. Her internist prescribes home oxygen 'as needed for shortness of breath.'
rationale_note: Breathlessness with normal saturation at rest, exertion, and sleep and no cor pulmonale.

vignette: 73-year-old man with severe peripheral arterial disease and a non-healing ischemic ulcer of the left foot. Pulse oximetry on the left toes reads 84%, while a physician-ordered arterial blood gas at rest on room air, evaluated by his vascular surgeon, shows PaO2 88 mm Hg and a right-finger SpO2 of 97%. The vascular surgeon prescribes home oxygen to improve oxygen delivery to the foot.
rationale_note: Desaturation is limited to an ischemic limb from severe PVD; systemic oxygenation is normal.

vignette: 82-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer to bone, enrolled in hospice. He has bone pain but no lung involvement and no dyspnea. His hospice physician ordered and evaluated resting room-air oximetry, SpO2 95%. The family asks for home oxygen for comfort, and the hospice physician prescribes it.
rationale_note: Terminal illness that does not affect breathing, with normal saturation.

vignette: 77-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and progressive dyspnea on exertion. Her pulmonologist's note states 'hypoxemic, needs home oxygen' and prescribes a stationary concentrator and portable system. The submitted record contains the clinic note, a CT report showing fibrosis, and pulmonary function tests, but no arterial blood gas or oximetry result.
rationale_note: No oximetry or blood gas result in the record; nothing shows the patient is not hypoxemic.

vignette: 72-year-old man with COPD seen by his primary care physician, who ordered pulse oximetry in her office and reviewed the result: SpO2 87%. The record does not state whether the reading was taken at rest or during activity, or whether he was breathing room air or using supplemental oxygen at the time. He has no angina, peripheral vascular disease, or terminal illness. She prescribes home oxygen.
rationale_note: SpO2 87% is recorded, but whether at rest and whether on room air is not documented.
